ai.title: Fix wrapper terminal reset for help output
ai.summary: CLI wrapper now conditionally applies terminal reset sequences to prevent `--help` output erasure. `resetTerminal` defaults to safe sequences (mouse/cursor/paste), only exiting alternate screen (`?1049l`) after interactive children or Windows crashes. Scope covers `cli/release-staging/index.js`, `cli/release/index.js`, and `freebuff/cli/release/index.js`. Added `shouldExitAlternateScreen` logic to detect signals or Windows native crash codes (`0xC000001D`, `0xC0000005`, `0xC0000409`).

eli5.text: When you run a help command (like asking for instructions), the program used to accidentally clear the text from the screen because it wrongly turned off the full-screen display mode. Now it only turns off that mode after running an interactive program that actually uses a full-screen display, so help text stays visible. It also recognizes when the program crashed unexpectedly on Windows and only then performs the full cleanup.

ai.title: Replace cleanup, meta, review skills with simplify
ai.summary: Consolidated three agent skills (`cleanup`, `meta`, `review`) into a single `simplify` skill. The new skill instructs the agent to review the entire change with fresh eyes to find design and implementation simplification opportunities. Covers the `.agents/skills/` directory.

eli5.text: The assistant was given a new way to check its work: instead of three separate review habits it used to follow, it now does one focused pass to spot places where a change could be made simpler or cleaner. This only affects how the assistant itself evaluates and improves changes behind the scenes, so you wouldn't see a new button or different output. If you looked at the project's instructions today, you'd find the old review steps gone and replaced by a single step telling the assistant to rethink changes with fresh eyes.

ai.title: Restore Carbon ads fallback
ai.summary: CLI ad logic now defers fallback ordering to the server. `useGravityAd` removes `fallbackProvider`; `chat.tsx` and `waiting-room-screen.tsx` drop `zeroclick` fallback. `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts` implements `providerFallbacks` map: gravity tries gravity, zeroclick, carbon; zeroclick tries zeroclick, carbon; carbon tries carbon only. Server persists impressions to `ad_impression` table with `onConflictDoNothing`.

eli5.text: When you see an ad in the app, the system used to decide which ad network to try first and which to fall back on right from your device. Now that fallback order is controlled entirely by the server, which tries Gravity first, then ZeroClick, and finally Carbon if the earlier ones can't fill the request. You won't see this change on screen, but you may notice more ads loading successfully because the server can coordinate across all three ad networks instead of your device giving up after two tries.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.96 ships web search rendering, GLM 5.1 removal, and VPN
ai.summary: This release bump to 0.0.96 packages all user-visible changes accumulated since 0.0.95, including a new WebSearchComponent that renders web_search tool calls in the CLI, removal of GLM 5.1 from the model registry and agent configs, and VPN/proxy traffic entering limited mode. It also includes the consolidated simplify skill replacing cleanup/meta/review skills, restored Carbon ads fallback with server-side provider ordering, CLI binary spawn error diagnostics with Windows guidance, numpad Enter interception in CLI components, split of public LLM provider code into @codebuff/llm-providers, CURRENTDATE placeholder for runtime template substitution, and chat completion concurrency logging. The terminal wrapper now conditionally applies reset sequences to protect --help output from erasure.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single version bump from 0.0.95 to 0.0.96 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, with no code changes. The commit metadata tags it as a release-bump, and the analysis notes confirm this commit ships all updates accumulated since 0.0.95.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.96 brings web search results right into your chat window so you can see where answers come from, makes numpad Enter keys work correctly when you're typing, and adds a new single 'simplify' skill that helps the AI review your changes for cleaner design. VPN and proxy users now get a limited-access mode that still lets them use core features instead of being fully blocked, and the terminal no longer erases help messages when things crash. The GLM 5.1 AI model has been removed from the free model list to focus on active models, and ads now fall back through Gravity, ZeroClick, and Carbon providers so you're less likely to hit empty ad slots. Upgrading means smoother keyboard input, readable search results, better error messages when the CLI fails to start (including Windows antivirus tips), and more reliable ad-supported free usage even behind network restrictions.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.679 release ships model removals, web search rendering, and ad
ai.summary: Version 1.0.679 is released across the `cli/release/package.json` and bundled with the Freebuff CLI. This release removes GLM 5.1 from the model registry and agent configs, adds a `WebSearchComponent` to render `web_search` tool calls in the CLI, restores Carbon ads fallback by deferring ordering to the server, and wraps terminal reset sequences to protect `--help` output from erasure. Additional changes include VPN/proxy users entering limited mode, numpad Enter interception, a new `simplify` skill replacing cleanup/meta/review, public LLM provider shims split into `@codebuff/llm-providers`, and a `CURRENTDATE` placeholder for runtime template substitution.
ai.evidence: Commit 2177c0ad modifies `cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the version field from 1.0.678 to 1.0.679. The diff is a single-line version bump in the release package.json with +1/-1 stats.

eli5.text: This release upgrades the Freebucks coding assistant with a smarter web search display, more reliable keyboard controls, and improved safety when you're using VPNs or public networks. Web search results now show up clearly in your chat instead of as hidden technical text, so you can read answers the same way you would a web page. The Enter key and numpad keys now work correctly every time, fixing frustrating moments where pressing Enter did nothing or submitted at the wrong time. If you browse through a VPN or proxy, you'll automatically get limited-mode access to keep things running safely, and Tor users see a clear sign-in screen instead of a confusing block. Ads that fund the free tier now have a smarter fallback system, so you see ads even if your usual source is blocked. Internal model cleanup also removed outdated AI options, leaving you with the most reliable models selected automatically.

ai.title: scripts/delete-user.ts Postgres deletion script
ai.summary: New scripts/delete-user.ts enables targeted Postgres user deletion via email or ID. Defaults to dry-run; requires --execute and interactive TTY or --yes to commit. Scope limited to Postgres: Stripe, BigQuery, and Loops remain untouched. --delete-owned-orgs extends cascade to org rows; otherwise execution halts if user owns orgs.

eli5.text: A developer can now run a behind-the-scenes tool that finds and removes a single person's data from the internal database using their email address or ID. The removal does nothing unless the developer explicitly turns on a confirmation flag, and even then the tool shows a plan of what would be deleted first instead of destroying anything immediately. By design the cleanup only touches the internal database, so payments, analytics, and email systems are intentionally left alone, and deleting the person's organizations requires an extra opt-in flag, otherwise the tool refuses to proceed if you still owns any organizations.

ai.title: Local agent discovery skips nodemodules, scripts, skills dirs
ai.summary: SDK `load-agents.ts` adds `shouldSkipAgentDirectory` to exclude `node_modules`, `scripts`, `skills`, and `skills-*` from local agent scanning. File filtering moves to `isLoadableAgentFileName`, which now rejects `.d.ts` and test/spec files via regex instead of simple suffix checks. This prevents non-agent files from being loaded during local agent discovery. Scope limited to `sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant looks around your computer to find available agent files, it now skips over folders named node_modules, scripts, skills, and anything starting with skills-, as well as folders that begin with a dot. It also does a more precise check on individual files so that type declaration files and any file named like a test or spec file are not picked up. You wouldn't see these extra files appear as agents anymore, but if you keep agent files in those now-skipped folders, they won't load at all. The change is live today wherever this version of the assistant tooling is installed.
